answer: Each identity holds one registered salmon hatchery on a tidal inlet fed by glacier melt: the registry logs its raceways; one hatchery backs one identity. It rears fry and releases pearl-silver smolts with coded tags; returns are counted at the weir; second claims are rejected. Each fake costs one real hatchery, 1,400 units and 180 days to the first return season; 100 fakes cost 140,000 units, 100 hatcheries, 18,000 days. Cheapest cheat: renting one for 900 units a season — the lender loses its own anchor, and bought smolts fail because their tags trace to another entry.
